author: Stone Fox Capital
title: As the stock market falls, companies that are active purchas
text:
As the stock market falls, companies that are active purchases of their own stock stand to benefit from lower prices. Based on recent proclamations from the CFO, Apple ( AAPL ) might be one of the biggest beneficiaries of the dip due to a massive cash balance. 

Bombshell Announcement Apple has dipped from an all-time high of $180 to close Monday at $156. The stock is down by 13% from the highs, but this is a dip that the tech giant actually wants. 
The company ended the December quarter with a cash balance of $285 billion and a net cash balance of $163 billion. Apple has to pay a repatriation tax of $38 billion, but the company has eight years to repay the amount so the cash balance isn't that impacted. 
Source: Apple capital return history 
This isn't exactly news for shareholders and history has shown the company conservatively returns cash to shareholders even despite the restrictions with foreign earnings. My previous research shows the company has made an intent of maintaining net cash balances in excess of $120 billion. 
On the FQ3 earnings call , CFO Luca Maestri dropped the bombshell announcement of the intent to eliminate the large net cash balance:
Tax reform will allow us to pursue a more optimal capital structure for our company. Our current net cash position is $163 billion. And given the increased financial and operational flexibility from the access to our foreign cash, we are targeting to become approximately net cash neutral over time.
The company announced the intent to provide the official update with the next quarterly earnings report in April similar to the updates of the last couple of quarters. The proclamation is meaningful since Apple has more flexibility now due to the removal of the restrictions on foreign earnings though the company wasn't exactly restricted from making similar moves in the past due to the ability to issue debt. 
Huge Impact After the dip, the market cap of Apple is down to $800 billion. Utilizing the $163 billion net cash position would repurchase 20% of the outstanding shares, or roughly 1 billion shares. The impact to EPS would be material. 
If not impressive enough, Apple should generate $60 billion in free cash flow this year. The total amount available to the company for capital returns this calendar year jumps up to $223 billion, or nearly 28% of outstanding shares. 
Over the last five years, the net stock buyback yield barely topped 9% back in 2014 when the market cap was closer to $450 billion. This yield was a positive signal of future stockgains and Apple could easy top that yield in the next year. 
AAPL Market Cap data by YCharts Of course, Apple is likely to increase the dividend and possibly utilize some more cash for acquisitions. To get to a neutral cash position, Apple will likely spend most of the cash on stock buybacks. Investors should want this outcome. 
Reducing the share count by 20% would cut the share count to 4.12 billion, down from 5.16 billion for FQ1. The $12.81 EPS target for FY19 would quickly soar to $16 per share. 
Considering Apple is unlikely to repurchase this many shares at the current price of $156, an average price of $180 (equal to the all-time high) would require $185 billion or about $22 billion of additional free cash flow this year above the current net cash position. After $15 billion in annual dividend payouts following another 10% annual hike starting in May and Apple could still end 2018 with $20 billion of net cash. 
Of course, different variations of stock buybacks will all be bullish to the stock. Spending only $80 billion would cut the share count by a large 10% at the current price. 
Services To The Rescue Lots of questions exists surrounding demand for the iPhone , but the story with Apple is quickly shifting to Services. The company reported revenues grew 18% YoY to $8.5 billion. Ultimately though, due to one less week in the calculation, service revenues per week were up 27%. The growth accelerated from the 24% rate in the prior quarter. 
Source: Apple FQ1'18 report 
The service revenue is now at an annualize revenue rate of $34 billion. The amount is in excess of 10% of revenue and importantly not reliant on selling new products since Apple ended the quarter with 1.3 billion installed products. 
Ultimately, the services growth provides long-term support for the stock valuation and being aggressive on share buybacks. 
Takeaway The key investor takeaway is that the dip is one wanted by Apple if the company does indeed intend to spend all of the net cash on share buybacks. One caveat is that the CFO made a contradicting statement later suggesting the amount spent in any fiscal year would continue at 100% of free cash flow: 
And when you look at our track record of what we’ve done over the last several years, you’ve seen that effectively we were returning to our investors essentially about 100% of our free cash flow . And so that is the approach that we’re going to be taking . We’re going to be very thoughtful and deliberate about it.
The stock trades at a 10 P/E ex-cash making Apple a huge bargain considering the Services revenue provides plenty of stable growth ahead. After a 20% buyback, the stock would trade below a 10 P/E. 
Unfortunately, the company isn't likely to be in a hurry to repurchase shares, but Apple is so flush with cash that the tech giant almost wants the stock to dip further. Investors stepping into the stock on any dip on Tuesday should get plenty of support from the company buying shares going forward, hence reducing the risk in buying at these levels.
